root_cause.text: Off-by-one errors in array bounds checks in the rkcif mipi register access functions where comparisons used `>` instead of `>=`, allowing access one element beyond the end of the arrays when the index equals the maximum value.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes comparisons from `>` to `>=` and replaces `_MAX` enum values with `ARRAY_SIZE` in `rkcif_mipi_get_reg()` and `rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg()` to prevent out-of-bounds access. For example, `block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE` is changed to `block >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace hardcoded bounds constants with dynamic ARRAY_SIZE checks to guard against out-of-bounds array access in rkcif_mipi_get_reg.
intent_record.what: Replaced hardcoded bounds constants (RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE, RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX) with ARRAY_SIZE checks on the mipi blocks and regs arrays, and changed inequality from > to >= to correctly validate array indices.
intent_record.how: Ensures that the block and index parameters are validated against the actual size of the arrays at runtime, preventing out-of-bounds access if the arrays shrink relative to the old constants. This makes bounds checking data-driven and maintainable.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace hardcoded maximum constants with dynamic array size checks to support variable hardware configurations and improve maintainability.
intent_record.what: Changed three bounds checks in rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg from static constants (RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE, RKCIF_ID_MAX, RKCIF_MIPI_ID_REGISTER_MAX) to dynamic array sizes using ARRAY_SIZE on the match data arrays (blocks, regs_id, regs_id[id]), and changed '>' comparisons to '>='.
intent_record.how: The bounds checking now adapts to the actual sizes of arrays defined in the hardware-specific match data, preventing out-of-bounds accesses when the hardware configuration has fewer entries than the previous static maximums. This ensures the driver works correctly across different Rockchip camera interface variants.

vuln_statements.explanation: Uses '>' instead of '>=' to compare index i against the number of blocks, allowing i equal to ARRAY_SIZE to pass the check, leading to out-of-bounds access on the blocks array.
Uses '>' instead of '>=' to compare index i against the number of registers, allowing i equal to ARRAY_SIZE to pass the check, leading to out-of-bounds access on the regs array.
